intended_object: The ideal-theoretic Artin map I_K → Gal(L/K) of an abelian extension of number fields L/K that is unramified at every finite prime. It sends each prime 𝔭 to its Frobenius and is extended multiplicatively to all invertible fractional ideals (Neukirch VI §7). The description comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition composes `artinHomAway` at S = ∅ with the identity equivalence `idealsAwayEmptyEquiv`. That equivalence identifies fractional ideals with multiplicity zero on the empty set with all invertible fractional ideals.

`artinHomAway` sends I to ∏ᶠ_v artinElementAway(v)^{count_v(I)}. With S = ∅, `artinElementAway` is the Artin element at v: the unique element of the Artin symbol's conjugacy class. That class is a single automorphism here because Gal(L/K) is abelian, and the library proves it is an arithmetic Frobenius at every prime above v. So the map takes each prime to its Frobenius and is multiplicative over prime factorization, which is exactly the Artin map. The library also proves the product formula, the value on primes and uniqueness.

The hypotheses are the right ones:
- Galois, plus the commutativity hypothesis `hab`.
- `hur`: unramified at every finite prime above every v.
Infinite places play no role in the ideal-theoretic map, so they are correctly ignored.

On generality: number fields are the standard setting for this construction. One could set it up for global function fields or Dedekind domains with finite residue fields, but the library's whole Artin-symbol infrastructure is built over 𝓞 K, and Mathlib has no general ideal-theoretic Artin map. So the definition is not too narrow.
